append.text: **Ps 20:9–13** (after 20:8 names the king in the third person, *Inveniátur manus tua … Pones eos*): the addressee is God or the king, and the Latin leaves it open (20:10 then names *Dóminus* in the third person). Kept **vós** — it holds both readings; the blind reader heard the Lord throughout, with the doubt the Latin itself raises at 20:10. *tu* (the king) is one touch away (decision `address`). For Gustavo.

Ps 20:2 = 20:14a *in virtúte tua* → *no vosso poder*; **20:14b the plural *virtútes tuas* → *os vossos poderes*** (the Latinist's MAJOR on the singular *ao vosso poder*: plural, and the object sung, not the addressee).

**Ps 20:14 *cantábimus et psallémus virtútes tuas* → *cantaremos e entoaremos em salmos os vossos poderes*** — D25's words with a direct object (*entoar em salmos* + accusative); the Latinist's fix *celebraremos* refused (D25).

**Ps 20:14 *Exaltai-vos, Senhor, no vosso poder*** (the Latin's order; the stylist's *Senhor, no vosso poder, exaltai-vos* against the echo poder … poderes refused — the echo is the Latin's). The Latinist at the gate (minor): the passive → *Sede exaltado* (option; refused — he grants the middle reading).
Ps 20:2 *exsultábit veheménter* → *exultará muito*.

**Transitive, God forestalling with good:** Ps 20:4 *prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis* → *vos adiantastes a ele com bênçãos de doçura* (the Latinist's minor on draft 1's *viestes ao encontro dele*: the anticipation; his *antecipar* is anticipáre's). Agrees with 16:13 *adiantai-vos a ele*; hostile *prævenire* keeps *surpreender* (17:19).
Ps 20:8 *non commovébitur* → *não será abalado*.
Ps 20:11 *Fructum eórum de terra perdes* → *Fareis perecer da terra o seu fruto*.

**Ps 20:11 *et semen eórum* → *e a sua semente*** — against this row, on the Latinist's MAJOR at the gate (*descendência* explains the image) and because the Latin pairs it with *fructum* (kept as *fruto*): the pair cannot lose one image. The second colon (*dentre os filhos dos homens*) tells the ear it is offspring. **Proposal for Gustavo: *semente* where the image is paired with fruit or harvest (20:11), and psalter-wide if the ear bears it; *descendência* only if the ear fails on *semen Jacob / Ábraham* (21:24, 104:6).**

**Ps 20:13 *pones eos dorsum* → *Porque fareis deles costas*** — draft 1 *os fareis dar as costas* (this row's image) and draft 2 *os fareis ficar de costas* fell to the Latinist twice (MAJOR: *dorsum* is a predicate noun; *dar*, then *ficar*, add a verb and make a posture). Draft 3 keeps the predicate noun in the *fazer de* build with the human back (*dorso* is an animal's or a book's); gate clean. 17:41 is a different build (the enemies' backs given to the speaker) and keeps its wording.
Ps 20:10 *Pones eos ut clíbanum ignis* → *Vós os fareis como um forno de fogo*; 20:13 *pones eos dorsum* → *fareis deles costas* (the *fazer de* build of 17:12).

Ps 20:5 *in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi* → *para sempre, e pelos séculos dos séculos*; 20:7 *in sǽculum sǽculi* at the head of the verse (*Porque pelos séculos dos séculos fareis dele uma bênção*). The Latinist's minors on the plural came on draft 1 and again at the gate — refused (D27).
Ps 20:12 *cogitavérunt consília* → *pensaram em desígnios* (the blind reader heard *pensaram conselhos* as advice).
Ps 20:12 *consília, quæ non potuérunt stabilíre* → *desígnios que não puderam firmar* (Ps 19:5's word).

**Transitive, *declináre in* + object:** Ps 20:12 *declinavérunt in te mala* → *voltaram males contra vós* (the stylist's worst line was *desviaram males contra vós*); the twin 54:4 *declinavérunt in me iniquitátes* should follow (*voltaram iniquidades contra mim*). *voltar* is also *convértere*'s — they do not meet in these lines.

**Ps 20:13 *in relíquiis tuis* → *nos vossos restos*** (obscure; Greek ἐν τοῖς περιλοίποις σου — another word than 16:14c's κατάλοιπα, so the split with *sobras* holds on D15; MS1932 supplies arrows in a gloss). *restos* here is God's remnant, not mortal remains; the blind reader could not place it, nor can the Latin.
Ps 20:7 *cum vultu tuo* → *com o vosso rosto*; 20:10 *in témpore vultus tui* → *no tempo do vosso rosto* (the image, unexplained); 20:13 *vultum eórum* → *o rosto deles*.
Ps 20:8 *rex sperat in Dómino* → *o rei espera no Senhor* (heard as trust first — the stylist's best line).

Ps 20:4 *in benedictiónibus dulcédinis* → *com bênçãos de doçura*; **20:7 *dabis eum in benedictiónem* → *fareis dele uma bênção*** (the blind reader heard *o dareis como bênção* as blessings given to the king — the Greek's dative, not the Latin's).
Ps 20:11 *Fructum eórum* → *o seu fruto* (paired with *semen* → *semente*).

terms: | decor | esplendor (*poreis sobre ele glória e grande esplendor*) | open | Ps 20:6; 8 lines (25:8, 29:8, 44:12, 49:1, 92:1a *decórem indútus est*, 103:1, 146:1 *decóra*). Kept apart from *pulchritúdo* → beleza, because 95:6 *Conféssio, et pulchritúdo* and 103:1 *Confessiónem, et decórem* are twins that the reader should hear as two words. *beleza*, *formosura* options |

| gáudium | júbilo (*o alegrareis de júbilo com o vosso rosto*) | open — **for a ruling** | Ps 20:7; 4 lines (29:12, 50:10 *gáudium et lætítiam*, 125:2a). *alegria* is lætítia's (50:10 has both); *gozo* is heard sexually in Brazil. But *júbilo* was unknown to the blind reader and collides with *júbilus / jubiláre* (46:6 *in júbilo*, and 12 lines of *jubiláre*). Options *gozo*, *alegria*; *regozijo* also free |
| lætificáre | alegrar (*o alegrareis de júbilo*) | open | Ps 20:7; also 18:9, 42:4, 45:5, 85:3, 88:43, 93:19, 103:14 (grep) — the active of the *alegrar-se* of 20:2 *lætábitur* |
| fraudáre | privar (*e não o privastes da vontade dos seus lábios*) | open | Ps 20:3; 77:29 *non sunt fraudáti a desidério suo* (the only other line) will follow; *defraudar* is option |
| dulcédo | doçura (*com bênçãos de doçura*) | open | Ps 20:4; 30:20 *multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ*, 67:11 *in dulcédine tua* |
| longitúdo diérum | longos dias (*e lhe destes longos dias*) | working | Ps 20:5, as 90:16 *Eu o encherei de longos dias*; 22:6 and 92:5 *in longitúdinem diérum* will test it |
| clíbanus | forno (*como um forno de fogo*) | working | Ps 20:10 only (grep) |
| stabilíre | firmar (*que não puderam firmar*) | open | Ps 20:12 only (103:5 *stabilitátem* is the noun); kept apart from *confirmáre* → confirmar (19:5) |
